At 344 feet, Britton Hill is a summit in Florida. The Britton Hill Trail covers 0.4 miles with about 36 feet of elevation gain — a gradual walk with modest climbing.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 30.98347, -86.28179 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 220 miles southwest of Atlanta, Georgia. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

This trail is hikeable most of the year. Summer brings heat and humidity — carry extra water — while fall and spring offer the most comfortable conditions. Ice is possible on shaded stretches in mid-winter.

Know Before You Go

The Easy rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 0.5 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go.
